main_body: A leafy tree: a large rounded green canopy (rows 0-34) on a short brown trunk (rows 30-45) standing on a small grass patch.
top_band: Organic canopy: the upper canopy is a mass of lighter greens (L~111, rows 3-16 at x=16) with no flat horizontal band. The trunk base and grass patch are at rows 42-46. No distinct rectangular top band.
evidence: Organic tree. The canopy is a rounded volume lit from above, with lighter leaf clumps on the upper part and darker clumps toward the underside (rows 15-18, 25-28 at x=23). The trunk is a short vertical column beneath the canopy, with the canopy overhang shading its top. There is no flat or rectangular surface, so the front-elevation and rim-only failures do not apply. The tree reads as a normal 3/4 organic object.

style.evidence: Measured facts: the candidate has a median of 6 colours per tile and 13 distinct colours in total, against about 108 per tile and 427-567 distinct colours for the references. That is far lower. The canopy has about 5 green steps, but they are arranged as coarse, blotchy clumps without the per-leaf highlights and varied clump shapes of the Beodeul trees. The outline is a dark green tint (0% neutral), which is good. There are no flat fills (0% coverage), but the 13-colour palette makes the piece much thinner than the references. The trunk is a plain 2-tone column with a thin base, and the grass patch is simple. Next to the references it looks flatter and less detailed.
